requirements.text: The ESA sample submitted for approval with regard to electromagnetic compatibility shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark.
The ESA sample submitted for approval with regard to electromagnetic compatibility shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the type designation.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3 of UN R10 shall be affixed to the rear lamp where it is an electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.

The rear lamp, where it is an electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA), shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The rear lamp, where it is an ESA, shall comply with the requirements for radiated and conducted emissions when tested.
The rear lamp, where it is an ESA, shall comply with the requirements for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances when tested.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp (ESA) measured by the method described in Annex 7 shall not exceed 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, the limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp (ESA) measured by the method described in Annex 7 shall not exceed 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, the limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp (ESA) measured by the method described in Annex 7 shall not exceed a constant 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp, as an ESA representative of its type, shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8 for narrowband electromagnetic interference.

The narrowband electromagnetic emission of the rear lamp, measured using the method described in Annex 8, shall not exceed a limit of 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

The narrowband electromagnetic emission of the rear lamp, measured using the method described in Annex 8, shall not exceed a limit of 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz.

The narrowband electromagnetic emission of the rear lamp, measured using the method described in Annex 8, shall not exceed a constant limit of 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The narrowband measured value of the rear lamp, as an ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances of the rear lamp, as an ESA representative of its type, shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp, as an ESA representative of its type, shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The rear lamp shall withstand the test severity levels of Table 2a in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band when tested by the method(s) described in Annex 9: stripline 60 V/m (20 to 400 MHz), TEM cell 75 V/m (20 to 400 MHz), BCI 60 mA (20 to 200 MHz), ALSE 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz), reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).

The rear lamp shall withstand the minimum test level of Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band when tested by the method(s) described in Annex 9: stripline 50 V/m (20 to 400 MHz), TEM cell 62,5 V/m (20 to 400 MHz), BCI 50 mA (20 to 200 MHz), ALSE 25 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz), reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).
The rear lamp, as an ESA representative of its type, shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the rear lamp ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Table 3a, where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor.
The immunity of the rear lamp ESA shall be tested by the method according to ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Table 3b.

The rear lamp ESA shall meet functional status classification B for the starting profile (Immunity test level II, 10 pulses) in a 12 V system if it is related to immunity related functions and is operational during engine start phases.

The rear lamp ESA shall meet functional status classification C for the starting profile (Immunity test level II, 10 pulses) in a 12 V system if it is not related to immunity related functions or is not required to be operational during engine start phases.
The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system), level III, 500 pulses, with FPSC III.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses, with FPSC I if related to immunity related functions and FPSC III if not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses, with FPSC II if related to immunity related functions and FPSC III if not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with FPSC I if related to immunity related functions and FPSC III if not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with FPSC I if related to immunity related functions and FPSC III if not related to immunity related functions.

The rear lamp ESA shall be deemed to comply with the broadband and narrowband radiated emission requirements and with Annexes 5 and 8 where it does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz.
The rear lamp ESA with no immunity related functions shall be deemed to comply with the requirements for immunity to radiated disturbances and with Annex 9.

The rear lamp ESA shall be deemed to comply with the requirement for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines where it is not switched, contains no switches or does not include inductive load.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA measured by the method of Annex 7 shall not exceed 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA measured by the method of Annex 7 shall not exceed 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA measured by the method of Annex 7 shall not exceed a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured broadband values of the rear lamp ESA, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the rear lamp on 12 / 24 V supply lines shall meet the levels given in Table 18 when tested according to ISO 7637-2:2011 as described in Annex 10.

The rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be immune to transient disturbances conducted along 12 / 24 V supply lines when tested according to ISO 7637-2, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Table 20.
The rear lamp shall not exceed the emission limits when tested throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.

The rear lamp shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the combination covers the full frequency range specified for the immunity test.
The rear lamp, as an ESA, shall meet the requirements when tested for immunity in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The rear lamp shall meet the immunity requirements with AM modulation, 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The rear lamp shall meet the immunity requirements with PM2 modulation, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.
The rear lamp shall meet the immunity requirements with PM3 modulation, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.
The rear lamp, as an electrical/electronic sub-assembly, shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The rear lamp, as an electrical/electronic sub-assembly, shall limit conducted transients it emits to the vehicle power supply.
Each lamp that is part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall satisfy the provisions set out in UN Regulation No. 148 or in another Regulation.
Lamps not satisfying the provisions of UN Regulation No. 148 or of another Regulation shall not be part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
All the devices of an interdependent lamp system shall be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.
Every rear lamp device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings.
All markings on the rear lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The value of "a" for the size of the approval marking on the rear lamp shall be at least 5 mm.
The rear lamp approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number.
The four to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
On a rear position lamp that cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.

On reversing lamps that cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The rear lamp shall bear the approval marking.
The rear lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The rear lamp, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

The rear lamp, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s) where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s).

The rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control, a secondary operating mode, or non-replaceable light sources.
Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle.
Where several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
The approval mark in the module identification code shall be from the same applicant as the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used.
Where replaceable light source modules are used, the light source module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
Where replaceable light source modules are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
Where replaceable light source modules are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage of the module.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.

The approval marking of the rear lamp shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
The approval marking of the rear lamp shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.

The category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
The approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body if the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body.
The main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device where an outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

The size of the components of a single approval mark of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated rear lamp shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each rear lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the general technical requirements and the specifications set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148.

The rear lamp shall conform to the requirements of sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and the Annexes referenced therein) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, pertinent to each lamp and to the vehicle category on which it is intended to be installed, where verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The rear lamp shall be designed and constructed so that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the rear position lamp and stop lamp functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source) or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

The internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp, where incorporating a manufacturer logo at the request of the applicant, shall incorporate only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components, provided that all requirements for the specific function are fulfilled.

A manufacturer logo incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens of a lamp shall be only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer.
The enclosed light emitting surface of a manufacturer logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
Stop lamps and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and, when all light sources are illuminated, the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure shall be produced, with a note in the communication form stating that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).

The applicant shall declare, and note in the communication form, that the lamp is only intended for installation on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, where a light source category or type is restricted for use in lamps on those vehicles.
The design of the lamp shall be such that replaceable UN approved light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

The light source(s) holder for replaceable UN approved light source(s) shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, with the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applying and, where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s) applying.
Light signalling devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
The replaceable light source module of the rear lamp shall be designed such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
The replaceable light source module of the rear lamp shall be tamperproof.

The replaceable light source module of the rear lamp shall, regardless of the use of tool(s), not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

The rear lamp shall meet the photometric requirements of the device when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code.

The rear lamp, where it is also approved with LED substitute light source(s) at the discretion of the applicant, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements when measured with the LED substitute light source(s) prescribed.
The rear lamp, if not otherwise specified, shall meet the intensity requirements with the light source continuously lit.
The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of each light-signalling lamp of the rear lamp shall be determinable.
The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear lamp shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function.
The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear lamp shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear lamp shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

The intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear lamp shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function.
The rear lamp shall observe the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

Where the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

Where the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed to be satisfied if the specified interdependent lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

The colour of the light emitted by the rear lamp shall meet the colorimetric requirements when measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
The light emitted by the rear lamp shall show no sharp variation of colour outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function.
For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics shall be verified with the light sources present in the lamp.
For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be met for each light source technology separately.
The light emitted by the rear position lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 4 for each of the two samples supplied.

The luminous intensity of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp shall be permitted to be 6.0∙10^1 cd below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by the stop lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 7 for each of the two samples supplied.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity of the reversing lamp may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, where a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The rear lamp shall have no measured value that deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in the Regulation.
For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of the rear lamp shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12.

The minimum photometric intensities of the rear lamp in the various directions of measurement shall be at least the percentages of the required minimum intensities shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

Where a rear position lamp or a stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity of the rear lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction as a percentage.

For a reversing lamp showing substantial local variations of intensity on visual examination, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions.
The rear lamp shall conform to the approved type from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R148.
The chromaticity coordinates of the rear lamp shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148.
The rear lamp shall conform from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint to the requirements of the Regulation, if any, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.

The luminous intensities of the reversing lamp, measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements, where the reversing lamp uses a light source technology other than incandescent only.

The luminous intensities of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp, measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements, where the lamp uses a light source technology other than incandescent only.
The approval number assigned to the device type shall be marked on the device.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier and other markings, or for the approval marking and other markings.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark on the device.
Where the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark on the device shall follow the prescribed format.
The retro-reflective device shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

The retro-reflector, if it is of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings required for retro-reflective devices shall be clearly legible on the retroreflective device.

The size of the components of a single approval mark for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps in retroreflective devices shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The retro-reflector shall meet the requirements of the sections on general specifications and individual specifications, and of the Annexes referenced therein, of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 in force at the time of application for type approval that are pertinent to the retro-reflector and to the vehicle category on which it is intended to be installed, where verification at the moment of type approval is feasible.
The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and continues to do so in normal use.
The retro-reflector shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflector or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough.
Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
Where the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the unit and filter shall be designed so that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.

The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous intensity reflected by the red retro-reflector, when illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1= β2= 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1), shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

The retro-reflectors subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 shall meet the colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2., when examined at least one hour after the test.
The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values after the heat resistance test shall be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
The retro-reflectors of the first group shall satisfy the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

The retro-reflectors of the second group shall, if necessary, satisfy the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflectors of the third group shall satisfy the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The retro-reflectors of the fourth group shall satisfy the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).

The retro-reflectors in each group, after undergoing the tests, shall have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

The applicant shall specify, when applying for approval, one or more or a range of axis of reference, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of coefficients of luminous intensity RI.

The retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements with reference to each different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range, where more than one or a range of different axis of reference are specified by the manufacturer.

The illuminating surface considered for photometric measurements of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall be defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter.
The illuminating surface considered for photometric measurements of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall be limited to 100 cm2.
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area of the illuminating surface to be used for photometric measurements.

The RI values of the red retro-reflector, when measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the red retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous intensity reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
The luminance factor of the red retro-reflective device, determined in accordance with Part 2 of Annex 4, shall be βv,R ≥ 0.03.
The retro-reflector specimen shall withstand the resistance to weathering test as specified in Part 6 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector specimen of the sample unit shall withstand the resistance to corrosion test as specified in Part 4 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector specimen of the sample unit shall withstand the resistance to fuels test as specified in Part 1 of Annex 7.
The retro-reflector specimen of the sample unit shall withstand the resistance to heat test as specified in Part 1 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector specimen of the sample unit shall withstand the resistance to cleaning test as specified in Part 1 of Annex 8.
The specimen of the sample unit shall maintain stable photometric properties when subjected to the test as specified in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The specimen of the sample unit shall resist penetration of water when subjected to the test as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6.
Where adhesive materials are used, the specimen of the sample unit shall meet the bonding strength test as specified in Part 2 of Annex 8.
The retro-reflective device shall be made of material coloured red in the mass.

The trichromatic co-ordinates of the red reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflective device, tested for night-time colour according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1, shall be within the specified limits.
The specimen shall resist weathering when subjected to the test as specified in Part 6 of Annex 6.
A specimen of the retro-reflecting device sample unit shall withstand the resistance to fuels test as specified in Part 1 of Annex 7.
A specimen of the retro-reflecting device sample unit shall withstand the resistance to heat test as specified in Annex 9.
A specimen of the retro-reflecting device sample unit shall withstand the resistance to penetration of water test as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6.

The rear lamp shall satisfy the conformity requirements from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflective device shall be complied with.

The retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" shall, at an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° or the angle specified for the device, and an angle of divergence of 20', conform in its position of minimum RI, obtained by rotation about its axis of reference, to the RI value specified for the device.

The retro-reflector marked "TOP" shall have an RI that does not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed during rotation about its axis by ±5°, with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° or the angle specified in paragraph 4 of the Regulation and an angle of divergence of 20'.
The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The shape of the light emitting surfaces of the retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors, from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The light emitting surface of the retro-reflective device shall be at least 25 cm2.
The moulded plastics reflector of the retro-reflective device shall withstand 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat test, the retro-reflective device and, in particular, its optical component shall show no visible cracking or appreciable distortion.

The retro-reflective device, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface, repeated after turning it through 180°, followed by immediate immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the retro-reflector after the immersion test, and the device shall not be considered to have passed if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water.

Where visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the retro-reflector shall meet the RI requirements when measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation after being lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
The retro-reflector's drain holes and other openings, where fitted, shall remain open during the water spray test.
Drain wicks, where used in the rear lamp, shall be tested in the device during the water spray test.

The signalling or lighting functions reciprocally incorporated or grouped with the retro-reflector shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF during the water spray test.
The rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflector shall withstand the water spray test lasting 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).

The interior of the rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflector shall not show a standing pool of water after the water spray test and drain period, nor one which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
The retro-reflector RI of the rear lamp shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after the water spray test.
The retro-reflector shall retain its RI, measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of the Regulation, upon completion of the dust exposure test.

Retro-reflective devices shall be designed so that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The front surface of the retro-reflective device shall resist tarnishing and the protection of the rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly where an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall withstand, stripped of all removable parts, a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

Retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion shall withstand saline mist produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
The retro-reflective device sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device immediately after completion of the corrosion test.
The retro-reflective device samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 500 hours.

After the outer surface of the retro-reflective device, in particular the illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol and about five minutes have passed, the surface shall not show any apparent surface changes when inspected visually, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

A retro-reflective device test sample smeared with a mixture of detergent lubricating oil and graphite shall be easily cleaned without damage to the retro-reflective surface when wiped with a mild aliphatic solvent such as n-heptane, followed by washing with a neutral detergent.

When subjected to continuous spraying for 60 seconds on the test component in its normal mounting conditions at a water/wash solution pressure of 8 ± 0.2 MPa, temperature of 60 +0/-5 °C and flow rate of 7 ± 1 l/min, with a 40-degree wide fan nozzle tip at 600 ± 20 mm from the retro-reflective surface and held at no greater angle than 45 degrees from perpendicular, the retro-reflective device shall show no damage to the retro-reflective surface, no delamination from the substrate and no separation from the sample mounting surface.
Where the outer lens of the lamp is textured, the declared light emitting surface shall be all or part of the exterior surface of the outer lens.
Where the outer lens of the lamp is non-textured, the light emitting surface shall be as declared on the drawing by the manufacturer, and the outer lens may be disregarded.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and indelible.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The lamps shall be fitted such that it is not possible for them to be inadvertently maladjusted.
The reference axis of the rear lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The reference axis of the rear lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with when fitting the rear lamp.
Rear lamps constituting a pair shall, in the absence of specific instructions, have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the requirements for lamps constituting a pair shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

Where a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated functions and the rear position lamp are switched ON.

Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.

Single lamps whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts shall be installed such that the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis, occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or such that the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent or tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.

Single lamps composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors shall be installed such that the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, or such that the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps defined as interdependent lamp systems under subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements applicable to single lamps whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts.
Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The photometric characteristics of a lamp (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON, in the absence of specific instructions.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

The apparent surface of the red rear lamp shall not be directly visible towards the front of the vehicle to an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle.

In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front by the rear lamp, as verified during type approval of the lamps, shall be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps if they exist, the side-marker lamps if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system including the rear position lamp, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The rear lamp functions shall not be concealed.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.
The number of rear lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of the Regulation.

Where the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

Where the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on a movable component, the inwards geometric visibility requirement shall be deemed satisfied if the interdependent lamp(s) conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
The replacement device for a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp shall remain operational in its original safety function.
During a temporary replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard shall indicate occurrence of the temporary replacement and need for repair.

Where rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control responding simultaneously to one or more of the specified conditions, the intensity of all such lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

Where rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control responding simultaneously to one or more of the specified conditions, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions in the entire intensity range.
Where rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

Where electric power supply conditions are not covered by the case of devices tested with a special power supply, secondary operating mode or applicant-requested voltage, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

There shall be no obstacle to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility, except obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.

Where, when the rear lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
For an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

All rear lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
Where the rear lamp is a light-signalling lamp incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Where the rear lamp is installed on a vehicle approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128, it shall be fitted only with light sources approved according to these light source categories.
Lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) shall be used exclusively where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8 is present and positive.
Lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) shall bear the marking related to the use of LED substitute light source(s).

The reversing lamp, where its luminous intensity exceeds 8.00∙103 cd, shall either be switched OFF or have its luminous intensity reduced to a value less than or equal to 8.00∙103 cd when the windshield wiper is switched ON and its continuous operation has occurred for a period of at least two minutes.
The reversing lamp shall not negatively affect rear camera system performance as defined in UN Regulation No. 158.
The reversing lamp shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if the reverse gear is not engaged or if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The number of S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be two and the number of S3 or S4 category stop lamp devices shall be one.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For S1 or S2 category stop lamps on M1 vehicles, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except for optional rear lamps.

The rear position lamp shall be positioned above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative at the manufacturer's discretion and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed, the rear position lamp horizontal geometric visibility angle shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards, where the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane if the lamp is mounted below 750 mm.

For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative at the manufacturer's discretion and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed, the rear position lamp vertical geometric visibility angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, where the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5° if the lamp is mounted below 750 mm.

The rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres to be considered visible, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
The rear position lamp shall have a closed-circuit tell-tale combined with that of the front position lamps, except when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The rear position lamp shall have a tell-tale indicating failure if required by the component Regulation.
The distance between the rear fog-lamp and each stop-lamp shall be greater than 100 mm in all cases.
The rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the daytime running lamps are switched ON.

The rear position lamps may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain switched OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
Where more than one rear lamp function is a manoeuvring lamp, the rear mounted manoeuvring lamp shall be mounted at the rear of the vehicle.
Manoeuvring lamps on a motor vehicle shall be connected so that they cannot be switched ON unless the main-beam headlamps or the dipped-beam headlamps are switched ON at the same time.

The manoeuvring lamps of a motor vehicle shall be switched ON automatically for slow manoeuvres up to 15 km/h where, prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the propulsion system, reverse gear is engaged, or a camera-based system which assists parking manoeuvres is operating.
The manoeuvring lamps of a motor vehicle shall be automatically switched OFF if the forward speed of the vehicle exceeds 15 km/h.
The manoeuvring lamps of a motor vehicle shall remain switched OFF after automatic switch OFF until the switch ON conditions are met again.

The apparent surface of the manoeuvring lamps shall not be directly visible to an observer moving on the boundary of a zone formed by transverse planes 10 m from the front and 10 m from the rear of the vehicle and two longitudinal planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle, these planes extending from 1 m to 3 m above and parallel to the ground.
Stop lamps shall not be used to provide the answer-back signal.
The position of the rear lamp in width, in height and in length shall comply with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of UN R48.
The measured distances for the position of each lamp of the rear lamp shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to that lamp.

The angles of geometric visibility of each lamp of the rear lamp shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to that lamp, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted for the mounting of light-signalling devices.
The rear lamp shall not allow red light to be visible towards the front, and shall not allow white light to be visible towards the rear, in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of UN R48.

The lamps of the rear lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle shall function in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp when switched on.

The tell-tales associated with the lamps of the rear lamp shall function in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
